<FeatureHeader id="x_admin_audit" />

## What it does

Makes the audit trail browsable from the WebHub for both audiences. A group admin
reads their own group's trail through `GET /groups/{group_id}/audit`, now
filterable by `surface`, `since` and `until` as well as `action` and
`actor_user_id`. A bot owner reads the fleet-wide trail through the new
`GET /admin/audit`, filterable by group as well, with each event carrying its
`group_id` and `group_title`. Both are newest-first keyset pages.

## Behaviour that must not change

**`next_before` means "there is more".** It is the id of the last returned event
only when an older matching row exists, otherwise `null`. The old rule (set
whenever a page was full) handed the client a trailing empty page.

**`/admin/audit` is owner-only.** The caller must be a bot admin (403 otherwise,
not 404, as for the rest of `/admin`) and the token must carry both `admin:read`
and `audit:read`. Rows are scoped to the caller's tenant through `groups.tenant_id`.

**Windows are half-open.** `since` is inclusive, `until` exclusive, naive
datetimes are UTC, and `since >= until` is a 400 `invalid_window`.

**Known gap (D2), preserved.** `administers()` does not honour `CB_OWNER_ID`, so
an owner who is not a group admin gets a 404 on the per-group route and uses
`/admin/audit?group_id=` instead.

**The second cross-shard read.** After `x_admin_api`, this is the only query that
does not filter on `group_id` (unless `group_id` is given, when it is single-shard).
It is keyset plus `LIMIT`, so each shard returns at most `limit + 1` rows, served
by the `id DESC` index from migration `0011`. Owner-only and off the reply path.

## How to verify it

`qa/integration/test_audit_log.py` (filters, exact cursor, fleet paging, tenant
isolation, `Task Count: 1` for the single-group reads),
`packages/cb-api/tests/test_group_endpoints.py`,
`packages/cb-api/tests/test_admin_endpoints.py`, `qa/api/test_contract.py`.
There is no Telegram surface, so no acceptance scenario.
